claims.statement: FPT/GHEC Pages custom-domain verification binds publication to repositories owned by verifying personal account or organization; it covers the domain and immediate subdomains, not every descendant hostname or general DNS ownership enforcement.

Unverified dangling Pages configuration can permit takeover after repository deletion, plan downgrade or other unlink/disable changes while DNS remains pointed to Pages. Verification is a source-described mitigation, not proof all lifecycle/DNS risks are eliminated.

Wildcard DNS is strongly discouraged: verifying apex protects immediate a.example.com but not deeper b.a.example.com under wildcard. Do not treat verified status as recursive wildcard coverage or authority to remove unrelated DNS records.

Organization/enterprise domain verification for profile badge and GHEC email-notification restriction is separately scoped from Pages verification. A Verified profile badge must not be promoted to Pages ownership protection or accepted DNS clearance.

Verifying a domain owned by the verifier but used by another unverified account/organization immediately releases it from the other Pages websites. Another already-verified owner's domain cannot be released this way; ownership and impact checks are mandatory before any approved native action.

Personal Pages domain verification lives in profile settings, not repository settings. Add domain yields a challenge DNS TXT record to create at hosting provider; UI creation does not prove control, ownership or successful verification.

DNS propagation may be immediate or take up to 24 hours. dig challenge-USERNAME TXT is a read-only diagnostic example requiring actual user/domain substitution; TXT presence alone does not certify native Verified state or live protected behavior.

Organization owners verify through organization settings/Pages, with organization-specific challenge TXT rather than repository settings. Organization membership or repository admin alone does not satisfy documented organization-owner authority.

After DNS propagation, Continue verifying/Verify completes the UI procedure; keep challenge TXT in DNS to maintain verified status. Deleting challenge after a screenshot is not a durable verification strategy.

No DNS challenge, release, verification, repository/site deletion, billing or publication change performed. Linked provider/domain/profile/enterprise guides remain separately scoped; source claims do not independently certify published assurance, actual anti-takeover behavior, rights or accepted policy.
